name: kerf_apply
description: Apply a batch of edit ops to the current Kerf document, atomically. Returns ok, the updated summary (every component with resolved x/y extents in feet-inches) and diagnostics. If any op fails nothing changes; read the error, fix, resend. For a brand-new detail send one {"op":"set","path":"doc","value":{...whole document...}}; afterwards prefer small add/update/remove ops so the designer sees clean diffs. Ops: add (path components | views | views/<id>/annotations, value), update (path components/<id> | views/<id> | views/<id>/annotations/<id> | meta, value = JSON merge patch, null deletes a key), remove (path to one item), set (path doc).

why.description: One short line for the designer's change log, e.g. 'Add HETA20 embedded truss anchor'.

name: kerf_inspect
description: Read the current document without changing it. q: 'summary' (component table + diagnostics), 'component' (resolved params, parts, every anchor with coordinates, z range; needs id), 'anchors' (needs id), 'at' (components under point [x,y] in view), 'catalog' (one component type's params and anchors; needs type), 'doc' (full JSON).

name: kerf_render
description: Render a view exactly as it will export and return it as an image so you can check your work: overlaps, gaps, leader clutter, notes pointing at the wrong thing, proportions vs the designer's reference screenshot. Call after every significant change and before telling the designer you are done.

mode.description: view = cropped drawing (default); sheet = full page with title block.
